question: When the applied force is fixed, the pressure p (Pa) is inversely proportional to the area S (m²) over which the force acts. When \(S=0.2\), \(p=500\). Find p when \(S=0.5\). (Unit: Pa)

provenance.contribution: Existing attributed explanation retained; project contribution is review and annotations.
provenance.reviewStatus: Current explanation retained and independently AI-reviewed; not teacher reviewed

solutionMethods.explanation:
The area increases by a factor of \(0.5/0.2=5/2\). For quantities in inverse proportion, multiplying one quantity by a positive factor divides the other by that factor, keeping their product fixed. Thus the pressure becomes
\[
p=500\div\frac52=500\times\frac25=200\ \text{Pa}.
\]
solutionMethods.label: Scale the pressure inversely

reference.question: When the applied force is fixed, the pressure p (Pa) is inversely proportional to the area S (m²) over which the force acts. When \(S=0.2\), \(p=500\). Find p when \(S=0.5\). (Unit: Pa)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Find the fixed product

\(p=k/S\), and \(k=0.2\times500=100\), so \(p=100/S\). When \(S=0.5\), \(p=100/0.5=200\).

Method 2: Scale the pressure inversely

The area increases by a factor of \(0.5/0.2=5/2\). For quantities in inverse proportion, multiplying one quantity by a positive factor divides the other by that factor, keeping their product fixed. Thus the pressure becomes
\[
p=500\div\frac52=500\times\frac25=200\ \text{Pa}.
\]
